## Approach

The operations are a monoid congruence generated by `(xx) = xx`. The rule `(xx) → xx` is length-decreasing, and its left side has no self-overlaps (no proper suffix of `(xx)` is a prefix of it), so the rewriting system is confluent. Each string therefore has a unique normal form, and A can become B exactly when their normal forms are equal.

To compute the normal form, scan left to right with a stack. Whenever the top four stack characters form `(xx)`, replace them with `xx`. Then output Yes if the normal forms of A and B match.

Hand-checked examples:
- `(x)x` has normal form `(x)x`, and `(xx)` reduces to `xx`, so the answer is No (this matches sample case 2).
- `(((((xx)))))x` reduces to `xxx`, and `x((((((((((xx))))))))))` also reduces to `xxx`, so the answer is Yes (this matches sample case 5).
